title: A Black Hole
subtitle: What if you fell in?
yt_title: What If You Fell Into a Black Hole? 🕳️ | Ep. 11 #shorts
description:
Episode 11 of a daily journey through the universe. 🕳️
We fall toward a black hole: gravity so strong light can't escape, spaghettification, frozen time, the first photo of a black hole, and how small our Sun would be as one.

➡️ Tomorrow, Episode 12: Next stop, a neutron star. One teaspoon weighs a billion tons.
Start from Episode 1 "Leaving Earth" on the channel.
Follow so you don't miss a stop. A new episode every day.

Images: NASA (public domain)
Narration: AI voice

#space #blackhole #astronomy #shorts #science

segments.text: Episode eleven. Next stop... a black hole.
A black hole is a place where gravity is so strong that nothing, not even light, can escape.
segments.headline: Not even light escapes

visual.commons: black hole accretion disk artist impression

segments.text: Fall in feet first, and gravity pulls your feet much harder than your head. You'd be stretched like spaghetti. Scientists really call it spaghettification.
segments.headline: Spaghettification

segments.text: Time slows down near the edge. To a friend watching from far away, you'd seem to freeze there, and slowly fade from view.
segments.headline: Time slows down

segments.text: The biggest black holes weigh billions of times more than our Sun.

visual.label: of Suns in the biggest ones

segments.text: In twenty nineteen, we finally saw one. This black hole sits fifty-five million light-years away, in the galaxy M87.
segments.headline: First photo: 2019

visual.query: M87 black hole Event Horizon Telescope

segments.text: And if our Sun became a black hole, it would be only about six kilometers across.

visual.label: our Sun, as a black hole

segments.text: Tomorrow, we visit what's left after a giant star dies. Next stop: a neutron star, where one teaspoon weighs a billion tons. Follow, so you don't miss episode twelve.
